title: Security & Compliance Review - Pen Test Results (Zenith Health)
summary: Redwood presents annotated pen-test results and remediation plan. Discussion covers critical/high findings, remediation timelines, vuln management process, secure SDLC recommendations, patching cadence, audit logs, RBAC/SSO, KMS/encryption, and SOC 2 artifacts. Agreed next steps include sharing detailed mitigation notes, scheduling a remediation validation window, and providing SOC2/ISO docs.
next_steps: Samir to send annotated pen-test report + mitigation roadmap (link) by 2025-11-21
Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary via secure link by 2025-11-19
Customer to grant temporary scoped access for remediation verification window 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-28
Schedule follow-up 30-minute call for remediation validation week of 2025-11-24
action_items: Samir Patel (Redwood): Provide annotated pen-test findings with severity mapping and suggested fixes (due: 2025-11-21)
Devin Ortiz (Redwood CSM): Upload SOC 2 and ISO docs to secure drive and share link (due: 2025-11-19)
Mark Rivera (Zenith): Provide list of internal owners and patching SLA per service (due: 2025-11-18)
Laura Chen (Zenith CISO): Confirm acceptance of remediation SLA and re-test window (due: 2025-11-20)
transcript: Header: 2025-11-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Devin Ortiz (CSM) — Laura Chen (CISO, Zenith); Mark Rivera (Security Eng); Jaya Kapoor (Head of Infra)

[00:00] Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — we'll walk through the pen test results, call out the critical/high items, then talk timelines for fixes and re-test. Laura, Mark — thanks for making time.
[00:18] Laura: Thanks. We mostly want to understand risk exposure and how Redwood will help verify remediations. We also have compliance gating to hit for an upcoming audit.

[00:32] Samir: Great. I'll share my screen — hope the PDF link in chat works, it's the annotated pen-test with reproduction steps. Quick note: some transcribed names in the report got munged, e.g., a couple references to the KV cache showed up as 'K V cash' in the auto-transcript, so ignore that — it's KV cache.

[00:50] Morgan: For context, Redwood ran an external vendor test last month and we got back the full findings. We triaged them into critical, high, medium. We're going to focus on the critical/high and the proposed mitigations and timelines.
[01:12] Mark: Can you confirm the scope? Which endpoints were in-scope and whether this included our private VPC deployment or just the hosted endpoints?

[01:25] Samir: Good question. The scope for Zenith was both — we had a hosted API surface test for the Redwood hosted control plane and an in-scope private deployment agent the team installed in their VPC for validation of the private connector. The report marks which finding applies to which env.
[01:45] Jaya: We saw an item about open S3 buckets — is that on our side or a Redwood-managed artifact?

[01:52] Samir: That one is an S3 misconfiguration on our side caused by a legacy staging bucket left with incorrect ACLs. We classified it as high; remediation is to update the bucket policy and enable block public ACLs. We've patched the config in staging and will apply to prod tonight per the patching cadence discussed below.
[02:15] Laura: OK, what's the CVSS and exploitability? We need to log this to our risk tracker.

[02:22] Samir: CVSS 7.5, authenticated-exploit is not required; it's basically a misconfigured ACL that could leak artifacts. We flagged as high because of data sensitivity — though no customer PII was observed in the leaked object set.

[02:40] Morgan: Another critical was the outdated third-party library in the inference runtime — that affects Dedicated nodes with an older image. We have a patch plan: bump library and run regression tests. That aligns with our secure SDLC guidance to stage, test, then rollout with canary.
[03:05] Mark: What's your patching cadence for runtime images? We need guarantees for SLA and notification windows before forced updates.

[03:14] Devin: Redwood's internal policy is monthly security patch windows for minor updates and emergency out-of-band patches for critical CVEs. For Dedicated customers we can offer coordinated windows; for Private deployments customers will control patching but we provide advisories and images.
[03:35] Laura: So for the vulnerable library, when can we expect images with the backport?

[03:40] Samir: We plan to push a patched image to our staging repo within 48 hours, run our regression suite over 72 hours, then schedule a canary for dedicated pools within 7 days. For private installs, we'll provide the patched image and a step-by-step upgrade doc — we can support via a runbook if you want us to handle the upgrade remotely during the window.
[04:05] Mark: We'll likely ask Redwood to assist since our infra team is PTO-heavy next week. We'll follow up on that in the action items.

[04:18] Morgan: On vulnerability management, we also wanted to show the lifecycle: discovery->triage->patch->deploy->verify. For high/critical we aim for 48-72 hour remediation plus verification on our side. We can tighten SLAs for enterprise contracts.
[04:40] Jaya: How do you handle disclosure to customers? If there is a vulnerability that could affect data residency or export controls we need to be notified immediately.

[04:50] Devin: We have a customer incident notify policy: initial notification within 2 business hours for critical, then follow-ups with RCA and mitigation. We'll include your security distribution list on that channel.
[05:05] Laura: Good. Next — encryption and KMS. There was a comment about key rotation not being enforced for long-lived keys used by the private connector. Clarify your KMS model.

[05:20] Samir: For hosted we use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys available for enterprise tenants; rotation is supported and we recommend 90-day rotation. For Private, you can plug in your KMS/HSM; we support both AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and customer HSM via KMIP. The finding was a config drift in one private test deployment where rotation wasn't enabled — that's configuration, not a technical limitation.
[05:45] Jaya: We'll want step-by-step guidance to onboard our HSM for key ownership. Also need to confirm whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext model context or customer payloads.

[05:55] Samir: Short answer: no plaintext access for customer-owned keys when using private KMS. For hosted API, payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest; customer data may be processed in the Redwood environment but we support customer-managed keys to limit access. We'll attach a diagram in the follow-up.

[06:12] Morgan: On audit logs and retention: the pen-test flagged gaps in log retention for admin API calls. We keep detailed audit trails but retention windows vary by plan. For enterprise we can extend retention and push logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders.
[06:30] Mark: Which events are exported? We need admin API calls, model version rollouts, key rotation events, and user management changes.
[06:38] Devin: Yep — we export admin API calls, RBAC changes, token issuance, model rollouts, and KMS key operations. We'll provide the log schema and a sample Elastic/QRadar ingestion config.
[06:55] Laura: The report also mentions RBAC gaps where a small set of service accounts had excessive rights. What's your principle of least privilege enforcement?

[07:05] Samir: We use role templates and offer scoped service accounts. The issue was a legacy service account created during early testing that had broad rights; we've marked it for decommission. We can also enforce an annual entitlement review and provide a report for customers.
[07:25] Mark: Do you support SSO/SAML provisioning and SCIM for user lifecycle to avoid manual role creep?
[07:32] Morgan: Yes — Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we can automate group-to-role mapping to reduce manual privilege escalation.
[07:42] Laura: Good. For SOC 2 evidence, we need copies of the Type II and the testing window. What's available now?

[07:50] Devin: We have our SOC 2 Type II completed for the previous 12-month window. We'll share the report PDF via secure link and an executive summary; note that the full report is under NDA — we'll require a signed NDA which we have a template for.
[08:05] Jaya: Also want to confirm the secure SDLC items in the report. Are PRs gated by static analysis? Do you run SCA, SAST, DAST in CI?

[08:13] Samir: We integrate SCA and SAST in our CI. SCA for dependencies runs on every PR; SAST runs on services in the merge pipeline. DAST runs on nightly builds for critical services. We also maintain a dependency freeze and require CVE checks before merge on high-impact services.

[08:35] Morgan: To add, we have automated policies to block merges if a PR introduces a high-severity SCA alert; there's a manual override that generates a ticket and requires approval by a security engineer.
[08:48] Mark: Nice. On remediation verification — you mentioned offering retest windows. How does that work operationally?

[08:56] Samir: We can coordinate a 5-day verification window where your team or our tester will run the checks against patched endpoints. For enterprise customers we can run the retest ourselves with a signed scope. The idea is to provide both an internal verification report and a scan artifact for your audit.
[09:14] Laura: Will you include exploit repro steps removed from public reports? We need something redacted for internal compliance.
[09:20] Samir: We provide both — a high-level summary and a reproduction artifact with sensitive details redacted; for Zenith we can provide a full reproduction under NDA.
[09:33] Jaya: A couple of quick specifics: there's a note about telemetry endpoints exposing debug headers. Is that an app-level bug or infra config?

[09:40] Samir: App-level; we had a debug middleware accidentally enabled in a canary build that leaked headers. We've patched the middleware to strip debug header output and added a CI check to prevent debug middleware in release images.
[09:55] Mark: Great. Any items that are still open and we should be tracking as highest priority?

[10:02] Samir: Two open criticals: the S3 bucket ACL (we're pushing fix tonight), and the runtime library CVE. Both are prioritized; we escalated to engineering and will send the patched image as noted. A few medium items are in backlog with 30-day SLAs.

[10:22] Morgan: Let's talk timelines quickly — we've proposed the following: immediate S3 ACL fix tonight, patched runtime image in 48h, canary within 7 days, full rollout 14 days. For private installs, we'll coordinate patching window and provide the image ASAP.
[10:40] Laura: That timeline mostly works; we need formal confirmation of dates in writing so we can align our change freeze windows.
[10:48] Devin: We'll send a mitigation timeline doc and calendar invites for the canary windows by EOD.
[11:00] Mark: On logging, can you provide an example of the audit log format and retention policy options? We need to confirm log immutability for 1 year minimum.

[11:08] Samir: We'll include the log schema; enterprise retention can be extended and we can support push to your S3 or SIEM. Immutability can be achieved by using append-only storage with versioning.
[11:22] Laura: One last thing — vulnerability management process: do you handle ticket creation and tracking in customer tooling or in your internal tracker?
[11:30] Morgan: We can do either. For Zenith, we recommend we create tickets in your tracker (JIRA) with read-only internal references in ours so you have ownership and audit trail.
[11:40] Jaya: Perfect. Anything else from Redwood side?
[11:44] Samir: We'll also attach runbooks for private KMS setup, a step-by-step for image upgrade, and the CI gating rules we talked about.
[11:55] Laura: Thanks. We'll review the annotated report and confirm owners. Expect us to respond with a prioritized remediation list by 2025-11-18.

[12:05] Morgan: Great — recap next steps: Samir sends annotated report and mitigation roadmap; Devin shares SOC 2/ISO docs; Redwood provides patched image and runbook; Zenith confirms owners and patch windows; schedule re-test validation week of 2025-11-24. Anything to add?
[12:25] Mark: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[12:28] Laura: Thanks — talk soon.
[12:31] Morgan: Meeting adjourned.
